item.title: Elderly man and woman lose lives in Navua crash
item.description: A 70-year-old man and a 67-year-old woman have lost their lives in a multi-vehicle accident in Navua. Police say it is alleged the victims' vehicle veered into the opposite lane, resulting in a collision involving three vehicles.
item.content:encoded:
A 70-year-old man and a 67-year-old woman have lost their lives in a multi-vehicle accident in Navua.

Police say it is alleged the victims' vehicle veered into the opposite lane, resulting in a collision involving three vehicles.

Four people travelling in the other two vehicles were treated at Navua Hospital before being discharged.

The bodies of the two victims have been taken to the Colonial War Memorial Hospital, where post-mortem examinations will be carried out.

Police are calling on all road users to take greater responsibility for road safety.

The latest tragedy has pushed Fiji's road death toll to 31, compared with 39 during the same period last year.

Police are again urging members of the public to change their mindset when it comes to road safety, stressing that keeping the roads safe is not solely the responsibility of law enforcement but of every road user.

They say fatal crash statistics for the first six months of 2026 show that speeding remains the leading cause of road deaths, followed by careless driving, drink-driving, pedestrians being at fault, improper overtaking and driver fatigue.

Police are also urging all Fijians to speak up against dangerous driving behaviour, warning that it poses a serious threat to everyone using the country's roads.

item.content:encoded:
Police are verifying claims of an alleged attempted child abduction at a school in Nausori after a social media post identified a man, who has denied the allegation, lodged a counter-report against the woman who made the post, and says he was at the school to see his daughter.

Following the circulation of the social media post, Nausori Police carried out initial enquiries and confirmed that investigations are continuing to establish the facts.

Police say more people are expected to be questioned as part of the investigation.

They have also confirmed that the man identified in the social media post has lodged a counter-report against the woman who made the allegation.

The man told Police he had gone to the school to see his daughter and not for the reasons claimed in the social media post.

He says he only became aware of the allegations after family members alerted him when they saw the post online, prompting him to lodge the report.

Police say the counter-report is also subject to the ongoing investigation.

They are stressing that investigations must be given time to be conducted properly and should not be rushed.

We have sent questions to Police to confirm whether the man's daughter attends the school and are awaiting their response.

The Fiji Police Force is urging members of the public to report incidents directly to Police and allow investigators to carry out their work before drawing conclusions.

Police are also reminding the public that the 1681 toll-free number can be used to report crimes, suspicious people or activities, as well as complaints against Police and concerns about service delivery.

item.title: Soqosoqo Vakamarama says surfing law must not encroach on qoliqoli owners' rights

item.content:encoded:
The Soqosoqo Vakamarama has called for the country's surfing law to be reviewed, arguing that indigenous qoliqoli owners should have a greater say over who is allowed to surf in their traditional fishing grounds.

Speaking on the Commercial Use of Marine Areas Bill before the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Justice, Law and Human Rights, President of the organisation, Adi Finau Tabakaucoro, says the current law allows people to surf in qoliqoli areas without the knowledge or consent of customary owners.

Adi Finau says the surfing law should not continue to encroach on the rights of qoliqoli owners simply because surfing is regarded as a tourism activity.

She says the current arrangement allows people to surf in traditional fishing grounds without the awareness of qoliqoli owners or nearby communities, raising concerns about how such activities could interfere with customary fishing rights.

Adi Finau describes this as the Soqosoqo Vakamarama's primary concern, adding that the organisation was otherwise supportive of the proposed Commercial Use of Marine Areas Bill .

During the hearing, committee member, Jone Usamate explained that the Bill would allow qoliqoli owners to apply for proprietary ownership of marine areas used for tourism activities or emissions reduction projects.

He says applications would be assessed by the iTaukei Land and Fisheries Commission, which would determine ownership and boundaries, and that the legislation was intended to replace the existing surfing legislation while retaining some of its provisions.

Committee member Faiyaz Koya sought clarification on whether the Soqosoqo Vakamarama wanted existing rights under the current surfing legislation removed.

Adi Finau responded that any existing rights that interfere with or encroach upon the interests of qoliqoli owners should be reviewed to better protect indigenous communities.

Koya then pointed to a provision in the Bill allowing the iTaukei Land and Fisheries Commission to renegotiate the terms and conditions of existing rights after ownership is transferred.

However, Adi Finau questioned the extent to which qoliqoli owners would be directly involved in those negotiations, saying the Commission did not necessarily represent the interests of customary owners.

She maintained that the protection of qoliqoli owners' rights should remain central to the legislation.

item.title: From teacher to trailblazer: Rupeni Rokoratu builds a Fijian fragrance brand
item.description: Creating a proudly Fijian perfume brand capable of standing alongside the world's finest fragrances a mission. This was shared by the founder of Perfume Fiji, Rupeni Rokoratu.
item.content:encoded:
Creating a proudly Fijian perfume brand capable of standing alongside the world's finest fragrances a mission.

This was shared by the founder of Perfume Fiji, Rupeni Rokoratu.

The former high school teacher stepped away from his career with a vision to create a proudly Fijian perfume brand capable of standing alongside the world's finest fragrances.

After eight years of dedicated research and development, Perfume Fiji became a reality.

Rokoratu says his perfume is crafted using natural ambergris and sikeci oil, ingredients traditionally valued by Fiji's ancestors.

He says his signature fragrance combines indigenous knowledge with world-class craftsmanship, creating a uniquely Fijian scent with global appeal.

He says his product is now proudly stocked at Tappoo Fiji, reaching customers both locally and internationally.

The former teacher adds that the brand is also preparing to expand into Papua New Guinea this September, marking another significant milestone in its growth.

Rokoratu's entrepreneurial journey was not without challenges, as access to funding remained one of the biggest obstacles until a 2025 grant from the iTaukei Trust Fund Board (TTFB) helped transform years of research into a successful commercial venture.

Reflecting on his journey, Rokoratu shared a simple but powerful message to dream big, but take action.

He says if people start today, they will get somewhere, but if they only dream and never act, they will never achieve their goals.

The iTaukei Trust Fund Board says that by supporting entrepreneurs like Rokoratu, it continues to fulfil its mandate of empowering iTaukei people through enterprise development.

The Board says that by investing in innovation, entrepreneurship and indigenous talent, it is helping to create sustainable economic opportunities that contribute to the long-term economic empowerment of the iTaukei community.

item.title: Residents raise alarm over rising crime in Cunningham following increase in robberies
item.description: Residents of Cunningham say they are living in fear as criminal activities continue to rise in the area, with a taxi driver becoming the latest victim after he escaped an attempted robbery and stabbing on Sunday. A resident says the incident happened at around 8pm when two young men flagged down a taxi and pretended to ask about the fare, but one of them reached towards the driver's pocket in an a
item.content:encoded:
Residents of Cunningham say they are living in fear as criminal activities continue to rise in the area, with a taxi driver becoming the latest victim after he escaped an attempted robbery and stabbing on Sunday.

A resident says the incident happened at around 8pm when two young men flagged down a taxi and pretended to ask about the fare, but one of them reached towards the driver's pocket in an attempt to steal from him.

The resident says when the driver grabbed the suspect to stop him, the man pulled out a knife and attempted to stab him, forcing him to let go.

The resident says the incident is another example of the growing crime issues affecting Cunningham.

The resident says one of the houses in the area has been robbed twice, with reports lodged to Police, but no arrests have been made.

He claims while Police do conduct patrols in the area, offenders often escape through multiple shortcuts within the squatter settlement.

The resident says snatch-and-run incidents have also become a concern, with many women being targeted for purse snatching .

He says the continued crime problems have left residents feeling unsafe in their own community and is calling on relevant authorities to take stronger action to address the issue.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Kasiano Vusonilawe confirms that the Divisional Police Commander South will be looking into the concerns raised.

item.title: After inspiring others to stay in school, 48-year-old graduates with IT qualification from Polytech
item.description: After seeing many young people who had not completed Form 5 while processing files during her time working in the marketing sector, 48-year-old Vonosia Rabuluwai decided it was never too late to return to school, and today she graduated with a Level 3 Certificate in Information Technology from Pacific Polytech. Rabuluwai, who is from Waivou, Rewa, says being part of the 350 graduates today is a pr
item.content:encoded:
After seeing many young people who had not completed Form 5 while processing files during her time working in the marketing sector, 48-year-old Vonosia Rabuluwai decided it was never too late to return to school, and today she graduated with a Level 3 Certificate in Information Technology from Pacific Polytech.

Rabuluwai, who is from Waivou, Rewa, says being part of the 350 graduates today is a proud moment after spending a year preparing for the course, including 20 weeks of practical training.

She thanked her lecturers for their dedication and the knowledge they shared throughout her studies.

Rabuluwai says she was fortunate not to face many challenges because her husband supported her financially and encouraged her every step of the way.

She dedicated her achievement to her family and her five children.

Reflecting on her previous job in the marketing sector, Rabuluwai says she regularly processed files and noticed many young people had not completed Form 5.

She says that experience motivated her to continue her own education and inspired her to encourage others to take advantage of opportunities to learn.

Rabuluwai says there is no age limit to education and is urging young people to take their studies seriously.

She also encouraged people who were unable to complete their schooling to consider enrolling at Polytech, saying it offers a second chance for those who missed out on education earlier in life to gain qualifications and build a better future.
